transcript.content: Hello. Welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately I can’t stop dwelling on how my face and body look as I’m aging, and it’s making me avoid things I used to do without thinking. It has just become really overwhelming recently, and I'm not sure what to do.
When you avoid these activities, is it mainly because you worry that other people will judge or scrutinize your appearance, or is it more about your own distress when looking at yourself?

It is really a combination of both, but the biggest hurdle is the dread of others seeing me. While seeing the sagging lines and my droopy neck in the mirror is deeply distressing on its own, the main reason I avoid presentations or going out is the overwhelming fear that everyone will notice how old and worn-out I look. On the worst days, I feel like I just can't let anyone see me.
Aside from these worries about your appearance, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or lost interest in almost all of your usual activities lately?

No, I don't really feel generally down or sad. My avoidance of these activities is entirely because I feel so self-conscious about my appearance and don't want people to see me, not because I've lost interest in them.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your appearance in mirrors, trying to hide or camouflage your face and neck, or comparing how you look to others?

Yes, most mornings I lose almost an hour in front of the mirror putting on and wiping off makeup, tilting my head, and zooming in on my face with my phone. I also constantly change my clothes to try to hide my neck and arms, and I keep asking my husband for reassurance about whether I look too old.

When you ask your husband or others for reassurance, do they tell you that these changes in your face and neck are normal or barely noticeable, even though you still find them highly visible and distressing?

Yes, that is exactly what happens. When my husband or people at work tell me they don't notice anything, it doesn't reassure me at all. To me, the sagging lines around my mouth and my drooping neck are incredibly obvious, and I feel like my whole face is collapsing regardless of what they say.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [F45.2, F40.1]. The patient has confirmed repetitive behaviors (spending an hour daily on mirror checking, taking photos, camouflaging her neck/arms, and reassurance-seeking) and that others do not perceive the flaws she describes. This presentation is highly characteristic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is classified under F45.2 (Hypochondriacal disorder) in ICD-10. Social phobia (F40.1) is ruled out as the primary diagnosis because her social anxiety and avoidance are entirely secondary to her preoccupation with her perceived physical defects.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent preoccupation with perceived physical flaws (sagging lines, droopy neck, looking old and worn-out) that are not noticeable or appear minimal to others. This preoccupation leads to repetitive behaviors (excessive mirror checking, camouflaging with makeup and clothing, and reassurance seeking) and significant functional impairment (avoidance of social situations and work presentations). These symptoms align with Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is classified under Hypochondriacal Disorder (F45.2) in ICD-10.
